insight.title: Your Wi-Fi Router Can See Through Your Walls
insight.subtitle: How your wireless signal maps your body in real-time.

sections.text: The Wi-Fi in your room is actually an invisible field that "sees" your every move. The signals don't just carry data; they bounce off your skin like ripples hitting a rock.
By measuring how these waves change shape as they hit you, computers can now map your exact location, your posture, and even the rise and fall of your chest.
This turns your router into a radar system. It is already being used in hospitals to detect falls through walls, seeing human movement in places where cameras cannot.
Your internet connection is watching you breathe.
